subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should installed SKILL.md metadata be allowed to declare autonomous scheduled or event-triggered agent execution, and under what operator approval and revocation model?
rationale: This cannot be resolved mechanically because the requested metadata changes the trust boundary for third-party skills and future autonomous runs, and it overlaps explicit cron jobs, plugin hooks, ClawHub metadata, and skill prompt semantics.

options.title: Design permissioned trigger contract first
options.body: Specify metadata location, operator approval, provenance, revocation, audit state, and scheduler ownership before accepting code changes.

options.title: Keep scheduling explicit
options.body: Reject SKILL.md auto-registration and document that skills may describe usage while operators create cron jobs or plugins explicitly.

options.title: Allow docs-only metadata now
options.body: Accept a non-functional trigger_description field for audits while deferring cron/event execution semantics.

recommendation.title: Design permissioned trigger contract first
recommendation.body: Specify metadata location, operator approval, provenance, revocation, audit state, and scheduler ownership before accepting code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans skill metadata, docs, security posture, plugin boundaries, and cron ownership, all areas where this history points to steipete as the best available routing candidate.
